messages:
opsbot: Pager: INF-Pool node NotReady spike in us-west-2, multiple inference pods restarting (pager severity: high) :rotating_light:

alex.sre: on it. grabbing logs + starting triage. affected pool = infer-prod-gpu-1

mira.platform: seeing kubelet restarts on node ip-10-0-23-14.usw2; journal shows repeated `kubelet: runtime: container runtime error` around same time as kernel OOM logs.

alex.sre: copy of `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200` (sanitized):
```
Mar 15 18:01:12 kubelet[1234]: E0320 18:01:12.123 kubelet.go:220] "Eviction manager: node has insufficient memory"
Mar 15 18:01:13 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 4321 (python) total-vm:5120000kB, anon-rss:4800000kB
Mar 15 18:01:13 kubelet[1234]: E0320 18:01:13.456 kubelet_pods.go:300] pod infer-abc crashed: failed to start container: runtime error: failed to create device: failed to allocate GPU memory
Mar 15 18:01:14 kubelet[1234]: INFO: Restarting kubelet (health check)
```

liam-infra: CUDA driver stacktrace in container logs for a few pods: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` followed by containerd OOM restart loop. looks like kernels/driver versions mismatched on some nodes after last kernel update.

incbot: Incident created: INC-2026-0427, severity P1. Link: <https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0427>

mira.platform: customer impact: elevated 500s for generation endpoints hitting that pool, p99 latency up ~240ms -> ~60% increase for some tenants. routing fallback has handled ~70% of traffic but some requests still land on affected nodes.

alex.sre: immediate actions: 1) cordon ip-10-0-23-14 2) drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` 3) scale up infer-prod-gpu-2 (fallback pool) by +3 nodes 4) create temporary routing rule to prefer fallback pool. executing now.

liam-infra: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-23-14` -> cordoned.

liam-infra: `kubectl drain ip-10-0-23-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` -> evicting pods. note: some pods failed to start on other nodes due to model cache size + mem footprint.

mira.platform: scaling fallback pool +3 requested to autoscaler, should be up in ~90s. creating temporary routing weight change to send 90% -> fallback.

alex.sre: quick hotfix: reduce model instance count to free GPU memory on target nodes and adjusted batch size from 8 -> 4 for the restless pool. patch applied to rollout config for infer-prod-gpu-1.

liam-infra: new nodes for fallback are coming up. k8s status: `kubectl get nodes`
```
NAME                          STATUS   ROLES    AGE
ip-10-0-21-10.usw2           Ready    <none>   12m
ip-10-0-22-11.usw2           Ready    <none>   3m
ip-10-0-23-14.usw2           NotReady  <none>   45m
```

alex.sre: logs from a failed pod (infer-runner-7):
```
E tensorflow: failed to init cuda: 'CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY'
E runtime: containerd: containerd: process exited with status 137 (OOMKill)
```

mira.platform: hypothesis: last kernel + nvidia-driver package update created a driver/ucm mismatch. nodes older than 1w fine, but nodes reprovisioned in last 48h are failing under top load.

sre-lead: pinging infra-eng to confirm whether recent imaging or AMI changes rolled out. @liam-infra can you escalate to image-team?

liam-infra: escalated to image-team DM, image-team confirms an AMI bake 48h ago used driver v535 but runtime expects v530 for our patched runtime. they're rolling a rollback candidate AMI now.

alex.sre: mitigation plan: (A) keep cordoned node out of service until reimage (B) reroute production traffic to fallback pool (C) increase eviction thresholds / set kubelet evict soft for memory on affected pools to avoid immediate OOM under burst (D) reimage node with rolled-back AMI when approved.

mira.platform: created temporary routing via console: route-infer-prod set: weight(infer-prod-gpu-1)=10, weight(infer-prod-gpu-2)=90. confirm metrics after 2 minutes.

incbot: Pager escalation: notified platform-oncall and image-team.

alex.sre: customer comms draft for SRE review: "We observed a NotReady/kubelet restart event impacting a subset of GPU inference nodes in us-west-2 causing transient OOM and CUDA errors for pods on that pool. We rerouted traffic to fallback capacity and are reimaging affected hosts. Some users experienced increased latency and a small fraction of 5xx errors between 18:01-18:06 UTC. No data loss. Full RCA to follow." Thoughts?

mira.platform: looks good, maybe add: "Affected requests were retried automatically by client-side logic in our routing layer" and call out time window.

alex.sre: updated and posted on incident page.

liam-infra: image-team approved AMI rollback candidate, starting reimage of ip-10-0-23-14 now. reimage ETA ~5m.

alex.sre: reimage in progress. leaving node cordoned until healthy. monitor.

mira.platform: monitoring: error rate for generation endpoint decreased from 2.1% -> 0.3% after routing change and scale up. p99 latency back down to within SLO for most tenants. still seeing intermittent restarts on remaining older nodes but no customer-facing errors.

incbot: Note: on-call handoff scheduled in 1h. current assignee: alex.sre -> handing to mira.platform at 19:30 UTC if stable.

alex.sre: quick post-fix checklist: 1) ensure AMI rollback rolled out to all reprovisioned nodes 2) add kubelet eviction tuning to infer-prod-gpu-1 daemonset config 3) add a probe to detect CUDA driver mismatch during boot and mark node unschedulable if mismatch. filing follow-ups.

mira.platform: filed followup tickets: TKT-2347 (AMI rollback), TKT-2348 (kubelet eviction tuning), TKT-2349 (driver mismatch boot probe). linking to incident.

sre-lead: good triage. Alex -> great job on routing + scale. Mira -> ensure customer_deployments list gets a post-incident note for any tenant who saw >1% errors.

alex.sre: handing pager to @mira.platform for next hour. leaving markups in incident page.

mira.platform: taking handoff. ping me if any new spikes. :thumbsup:

incbot: Incident INC-2026-0427 status: mitigated -> monitoring. assigned to SRE for RCA.

alex.sre: moving to postmortem drafting. thanks team. :heart:
